findings.title: Exhausted user-storage recovery codes are 'removed' from the wrong store; null id can crash the login
findings.body:
`RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` can now return a credential that came from the user storage provider (`getFederatedCredentialsStream`). When that credential reports `allCodesUsed()`, the authenticator still calls `removeStoredCredentialById(recoveryCodeCredentialModel.getId())`. For a non-local user this targets Keycloak's federated JPA credential store, not the user storage provider, so the exhausted credential is never removed where it actually lives.

It can also fail outright. The reference provider in this PR returns a model built with `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...)`, which has no id, and `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials` does not copy the stored id. The result is `removeStoredCredentialById(null)`, which reaches `em.find(FederatedUserCredentialEntity.class, null, ...)` and throws `IllegalArgumentException`. The user would get an error page when signing in with their last recovery code.

Fix: when the credential is federated, remove or disable it through the storage provider (e.g. `disableCredentialType`), or skip the local removal and rely only on the required action.

findings.title: Login page throws NoSuchElementException for storages that validate recovery codes but don't override getCredentials
findings.body:
With this PR a user storage provider can own the recovery-codes credential: it gets `updateCredential`, and `isConfiguredFor`/`isValid` are routed to it. The login page bean still calls `credentialModelOpt.get()` unconditionally.

`CredentialInputUpdater.getCredentials` defaults to `Stream.empty()`. A provider that implements `supportsCredentialType`/`isConfiguredFor`/`isValid`/`updateCredential` for `recovery-authn-codes` but not `getCredentials` therefore gets an empty Optional here (there is no local credential either). The recovery-code form then fails with `NoSuchElementException` (HTTP 500) every time it is rendered.

Even when `getCredentials` is implemented, the provider must return a credential in Keycloak's internal hashed `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel` JSON format, while it receives the codes as a raw JSON array of strings. This contract is undocumented.

Fix: handle the absent case gracefully, and document the contract or derive the next code number differently.

findings.title: Regenerating codes into user storage leaves previously stored local recovery codes valid
findings.body:
The previous code called `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider.createCredential`, which deletes any existing recovery-codes credential before storing the new one. When the user storage accepts the new codes (`userStorageCreated == true`), this branch only logs and never removes an existing locally stored credential.

Before this change, federated users' recovery codes were always kept in Keycloak's local/federated credential store. After upgrading to a storage provider that supports `recovery-authn-codes`, a user who regenerates codes will still have the old local credential. `UserCredentialManager.isValid` falls back to the local `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider` when the storage rejects an input, so the old, supposedly replaced codes can still be used to authenticate.

Fix: remove any stored `recovery-authn-codes` credential when the codes are successfully saved in user storage.

findings.title: getCredentials dereferences myUser without null check
findings.body:
`getCredentials` calls `getMyUser(user)` and immediately accesses `myUser.recoveryCodes` and `myUser.otp`. Every other method in this provider (`isConfiguredFor`, `isValid`, `getDisableableCredentialTypesStream`) guards against `myUser == null`.

`getCredentials` is now reached via `getFederatedCredentialsStream()` from the recovery-code login bean and authenticator. A user unknown to the in-memory map (e.g. removed from the map but still cached) would cause an NPE instead of an empty stream.
